newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish cabinet clears insurer PZU sale next year.
newsitem.headline: Polish cabinet clears insurer PZU sale next year.

text.p: Despite protests by the opposition, the government decided on Tuesday to proceed with its plan to increase the capital of Poland's biggest insurer PZU SA prior to its privatisation.

The government said in a statement that it would seek to privatise PZU, which dominates both Poland's non-life and life insurance market, next year. The firm's spokesman said this would probably be done through a public offering.

"The government... expects that the Treasury Ministry will take necessary actions to increase PZU's capital from non-budgetary sources and include the company in the privatisation programme for 1998," the statement said.

The opposition Solidarity alliance (AWS) demanded earlier this week that the plan be dropped, charging it involved a plot by PZU's management and some cabinet members to sell a large stake in the company cheaply to some domestic investors.
PZU rejected all allegations as political campaigning before the September 21 general election.

The firm's spokesman, Marek Maszek, said he hoped the government's decision cleared the way for a new PZU share issue, which would raise at least 600 million zlotys ($173.3 million) needed to secure mandatory safety ratios.
"After the issue, which would allow PZU to meet the required solvency standards... the full privatisation could take place next year through a public offering," Maszek told Reuters.

The Treasury Ministry's department director for joint-stock firms, Elzbieta Niebisz, said the ministry could stage the issue within a month if the government wanted to raise PZU's capital in this way.
"I do not know the government's decisions precisely... but I think that increasing PZU's capital from non-budgetary sources means a new issue," she told Reuters.
Niebisz said the ministry would consult PZU's management on the scope of the new issue and the number of investors that would buy it.

Solidarity, which hopes to defeat the ruling ex-communists in the September polls, has said that an issue to a closed group of investors before the firm's full privatisation is not necessary because PZU's assets could be revalued to enable it to meet the mandatory safety standards.
It says PZU's life insurance subsidiary PZU-Zycie is worth 10 times more than its book value officially stated as 150 million zlotys, and so if revalued the parent firm would meet all standards.

Solidarity insurance analyst Tomasz Truskawa said on Monday that PZU President Jan Monkiewicz and some cabinet members have been pushing the issue to sell the firm cheaply to two Polish investors: banking group Pekao SA and computer firm Prokom.
Truskawa said PZU's management had manipulated the firm's accounts, allowing it to report a loss last year to diminish the value of the firm and thereby the value of the issue.
"The whole game was designed to allow a certain group of people to take over PZU," Truskawa told a news conference, naming Pekao and Prokom.
PZU's Maszek said Pekao and Prokom were only two of many investors interested in the issue.

Truskawa said the government should promptly restructure PZU and sell it to a strong Western strategic investor lest PZU lose out to foreign companies when Poland fully liberalises its insurance market in 1999.
PZU was a monopolist under communism before 1989 and still controls 65 percent of the non-life insurance marker and nearly 80 percent of the life sector.
